rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Only the earliest pair is underresolved, while all peaks elute comfortably before 10 minutes. Raise temperature while keeping the gradient unchanged to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity separates that pair.

The temperature increase nearly resolved the critical early pair. Lengthen the gradient by one grid step to test whether a shallower slope brings its resolution above 1.5 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is established; now seek a shorter fully resolved run. Narrowing the organic window while reducing tG gives a slope between injections 2 and 3, which should preserve resolution of the early pair and shorten the last retention time.

Raise the starting organic fraction by one step while preserving injection 4's gradient slope. This tests whether the initial low-organic segment can be trimmed to shorten elution without sacrificing the critical early pair's resolution.

Return to the lower starting organic fraction that preserved early-pair resolution. This trimmed gradient is only slightly steeper than injection 4 and ends above the estimated last-peak elution composition, targeting a shorter run with full resolution.

Full-score methods are already established, so test the low-temperature selectivity regime against the same gradient used at 40 and 60 C. A reversal of the critical pair's elution order could provide another route to full resolution with a steeper, faster gradient.

Slightly steepen the successful 60 C gradient to target the fastest fully resolved run near the early-pair resolution boundary. The last peak should elute shortly into the final hold, so check whether the lower endpoint offsets the time saved.

Test whether 30 C separates the late cluster seen at 25 C while retaining the favorable early-pair selectivity at low temperature. The steeper gradient also probes whether this alternative selectivity regime can deliver a shorter fully resolved run.

Probe an intermediate-temperature route to a faster full-score method: 35 C may separate the late cluster, while the higher starting organic fraction tests whether early-pair selectivity improves in this temperature regime. The stronger start should also shorten retention.

At 35 C the late cluster is resolved and only the early pair falls short. Raise phi0 one step to test its effect on early-pair selectivity while slightly reducing gradient steepness and shortening the low-organic portion of the run.

Return to the successful high-temperature regime and reduce the slope relative to injection 5 to recover early-pair resolution at phi0 = 0.10. This tests whether a trimmed starting window can provide another full-score method with useful resolution margin.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a shallower gradient for greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Monitor both the first pair and the third–fourth pair, since the latter lost some resolution when tG increased previously.

Test a gradient just steeper than injection 8 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary at 60 C. The higher endpoint also avoids terminal-hold slowing, although the early pair may fall just below R = 1.5.

Slightly steepen injection 12's gradient while retaining its higher starting organic fraction. This tests the full-resolution boundary for phi0 = 0.10 and should shorten retention modestly, with the early pair predicted to remain close to R = 1.5.

Test a shallower gradient at 35 C to resolve the early pair while preserving separation of the late cluster. This explores a lower-temperature full-score alternative, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Interpolate between the fully resolved 12- and 16-minute gradients to balance the two slope-sensitive early pairs. This should retain maximum CRF with greater resolution margin than the fastest methods and shorter retention than injection 13.
